title: Node.js Patches Brotli Remote Code Execution Flaw: Find Vulnerable Runtimes Before Attackers Do
content_md: Executive Summary On October 21, 2026, Node.js released fixes for 10 vulnerabilities across its three supported release lines: 22.x, 24.x, and 26.x. Four are rated High. The most severe, CVE-2026-111497, is an out-of-bounds write in the bundled Brotli decoder that Node.js says permits remote code execution. These flaws live in the Node.js runtime itself, not in application packages, so dependency checks will not surface them. Qualys customers can find affected runtimes across hosts, containers, and cloud workloads, including copies outside standard install paths, prioritize those exposed to the internet, and confirm each fix after patching. Why This Release Needs Attention Now The four high-severity vulnerabilities impact two areas that nearly every Node.js service interacts with: compressed data and outbound connections. CVE-2026-111497 is a vulnerability found in the code responsible for decompressing Brotli data. Any service that unpacks Brotli content it did not create is affected by this issue. Additionally, there are three other high-severity vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-105482, CVE-2026-105483, and CVE-2026-106069. These vulnerabilities compromise Node.js’s ability to verify hostnames and certificates, which is especially important for services that connect to hosts on behalf of users.
